topic: Do four-day work weeks improve software-team delivery without harming quality?
quality_gates: Every non-obvious high-stakes claim has ≥2 independent high/medium-integrity sources or 1 primary.
Low-integrity sources used only illustratively, with explicit framing.
Opposing evidence is steelmanned, not minimized.
Findings dated as-of; rapidly evolving topics carry a monitor note.
Uncertainty bands appear on every key finding.
Decision-relevant residual risk is explicit if audience is executive/product.

layers.title: Layer 1 — Executive summary (150–300 words)
slots: Core answer in one paragraph, dated as-of.
Confidence band + top 2 drivers of uncertainty.

layers.title: Layer 2 — Key findings (claim + citation + confidence)
slots: One bullet per finding: claim, inline citation, source note, confidence tag, 1–2 sentence rationale.
Mark contested findings explicitly; do not smooth them.

group_by_questions.text: What is the current, evidence-based answer to: Do four-day work weeks improve software-team delivery without harming quality?
What are the strongest competing explanations or positions, and what evidence supports each?
Which claims are well-established vs contested vs unknown as of the research date?
What mechanisms (causal, institutional, technical) would have to be true for the leading claim to hold?
Who are the stakeholders, what incentives do they have, and how does that shape the evidence base?

seed_findings.text: Trial sites maintained or improved service levels while reducing hours by 4–5 per week

layers.title: Decision frame
slots: Recommended option and the evidence that would reverse it.
No-regret moves vs bets that need more evidence.

layers.title: Layer 5 — Limitations, uncertainties, research agenda
slots: Inventory of gaps and volatile areas.
Specific follow-up queries and data sources.
known_gaps: Q1: Missing source classes: primary documents
Q2: Fewer than 2 sources or no high-integrity source
Empty questions remain — do not synthesize a confident answer yet.

persona_passes_before_delivery: domain_expert: methods and missing canonical sources
anti_patterns: Leading with a narrative and hunting citations afterwards.
False balance on a lopsided evidence base.
Burying contested findings in an appendix.
Omitting the as-of date on volatile topics.
